reason: The 32-bit counter change is small and directly testable, though any gain is likely limited. Reordering ZA tile operations is also expressible, but carries some FP32 rounding risk. Scratch lifetime changes need careful stack auditing and have no demonstrated performance upside. B-panel packing and transpose fusion require larger coordinated changes with substantial correctness risk; repeated packing may offset any benefit. The two N=64 panel proposals are duplicates and both need a helper that is not supplied, so they rank last. No supplied measurement establishes a winner or a cause for noisy score changes.
